title: .21 per-row tool-path coverage, CHAT_COMPLETIONS wire (gemini-3.7-flash, the slim cc-wire row; live config api_backend=chat_completions, known open-compat issue family per .20/.35): two headless turns in one session. Turn 1 = baseline reply (carries the MCP server announcement). Turn 2 = the coverage turn: a REAL codegraph MCP round-trip (use_tool -> codegraph__codegraph_explore against the worktree index) AND a REAL plain tool round-trip (run_terminal_command echo). FIRST-OBSERVATION DISCIPLINE: the campaign's wire evidence contains NO chat_completions request capture yet (gen-matrix.py has no cc path; count_wire_model_calls misses it — gaps G1/G2), so the cc container shapes (tool_calls[] on the assistant turn, role:tool result message) AND the request path are RECON verdict pins here, not hard pins — they record the first live shapes for the .36 sweep to ratify (promote to hard pins after the first confirmed run, the RED-CLEARED promotion discipline). The where-filter is path-agnostic for the same reason. The DISCRIMINATING container-agnostic pins still force the real round-trips: the escaped-JSON-form use_tool call (arguments is a JSON-encoded string on the cc wire too — the same discriminating form as responses), the declared codegraph target, the declared echo command, and the reply-side payload proofs (echo output + classify_error file path from the real index result) — whatever container the LiteLLM cc layer puts the calls in.

steps.prompt: Perform exactly these two tool calls, in this order, and no other tools: (1) use the use_tool tool to call the codegraph explore tool (qualified name codegraph__codegraph_explore) with arguments query 'strip_model_bound_state classify_error', maxFiles 2, projectPath /Users/palanisd/Projects/upstream/wt/grok-build-responses; (2) use the run_terminal_command tool to run the command: echo T21-CC-GE37-ECHO. After both tool results are in hand, reply with exactly three lines: line 1: T21-CC-GE37-DONE; line 2: the exact text the echo command printed; line 3: the repo-relative file path of the file that defines classify_error, exactly as reported in the explore result.

ndjson.label: TURN COMPLETES: the merged event stream reached the end terminal (the tool-bearing turn did not die through the chat_completions wire).

MODEL DELIVERED: the final reply carries the DONE nonce (the model finished the turn and answered the reply protocol; the nonce is model-generated output, not prompt text, so it cannot be pre-seeded).

PLAIN ROUND-TRIP PAYLOAD (container-agnostic): the reply's line 2 carries the echo output the model read from the run_terminal_command result (the prompt names the command, so the wire grep alone cannot separate a real result from a parroted one; the sh_call discriminating pin plus this reply pin together close the loop).

MCP ROUND-TRIP PAYLOAD (container-agnostic, real-index proof): the reply's line 3 carries the classify_error defining file path as reported by the explore result. The path is NOT in the prompt and the crate is private (no training prior); the model can only produce it if the real index content flowed result -> model -> reply. 0 hits = the MCP result never carried real content (stale/empty index, wrong args, or server error) even if the call was emitted.

wire.label: CONTROL (harness premise, anti-vacuous pin): the codegraph MCP server's turn-boundary announcement ('MCP server(s) connected: - codegraph (N tools): ...') actually reached the row's wire — the rig offered the MCP tool. Pin is count-agnostic across codegraph builds (the 2026-09-14 capture read '(1 tool)', current build single-tool era; both match). 0 hits = BLOCKED/HARNESS (server never announced: startup failure, missing binary, config not inherited), not VACUOUS — no model conclusion is possible without the offer.

CONTROL (model premise, anti-vacuous pin, DISCRIMINATING FORM): a use_tool call was actually ISSUED — the pattern is the escaped-JSON form of the tool_name key (arguments is a JSON-encoded string on the responses/cc wire), which appears only in a real function_call's arguments; the tools[] schema entry (single-level quotes) and the prompt (plain text) cannot match it. Only use_tool carries a tool_name parameter (31-tool set verified, rt-m8 req-004). 0 hits = VACUOUS.

CONTROL (model premise, anti-vacuous pin, DISCRIMINATING FORM): a use_tool call targeted the DECLARED fully-qualified tool codegraph__codegraph_explore — the escaped-JSON form of the FQ name appears only in a real call's arguments; the prompt carries the name plain (single-level, unquoted) and the MCP announcement text carries NO FQ names at all (current codegraph build server-instructions verified: 0 'codegraph__' occurrences; the 2026-09-14 capture announce lists bare codegraph_explore). 0 hits = VACUOUS (wrong/absent target).

CONTROL (model premise, anti-vacuous pin, DISCRIMINATING FORM): the DECLARED echo command was actually issued — the escaped-JSON form of command+value appears only in a real call's arguments (the prompt carries the command plain; the tools[] schema line is "command": {). Matches run_terminal_command or monitor with that exact command; the prompt forbids other tools, and either shell tool proves the plain builtin round-trip path. 0 hits = VACUOUS.

MODEL ECHO (RT-M5 lineage): the NEWEST matched row request (nth=0 = newest under the runner's mtime-sorted glob) carries the row's own model id — no cross-model misrouting on the chat_completions wire. The session-title side call also matches the where filter (same body.model), so it cannot false-fail this pin.

VERDICT RECORD (evidence-only, machine-readable): the upstream HTTP status of the LAST matched row request, paired to its resp-NNN.jsonl by capture sequence. No status_in — a 400 on the tool round-trip is a tool-path FINDING surfaced by the round-trip pins (cg_rt/echo_nd/path_nd), and the session-title side call (it carries the row's body.model, so it passes the where filter; .29: it 500s proxy-side, sessions unaffected) may be the last match, so an assertive status_in would false-fail. Cc wire: first-observation — the last matched request's status is recorded as evidence; no acceptivity assertion until the first run ratifies the shape (RED-CLEARED promotion).

RATIFIED hard pin (first-observation 20260917T102912Z campaign, t21-cc-ge37-mcp-tool wire req-004/006/007/008: all four gemini-3.7-flash model requests on /v1/chat/completions, HTTP 200; Q2/Q3 ratify-then-pin pre-authorization, observed = predicted): the cc wire's exact request path.

RATIFIED hard pin (first-observation 20260917T102912Z req-007/008; stream-side container = resp-006/007 delta.tool_calls frames, escaped-frame text): the cc tool-call container is present on the request wire for this row (replayed assistant tool_calls[] history).
RATIFIED hard pin (first-observation 20260917T102912Z req-007/008): the tool result returns on the cc wire as a role:tool message carrying tool_call_id + content (observed 'exit: 0' + echo marker).

vacuous_if.note: MCP server never announced on the row wire — rig failed (startup/config/binary); no model conclusion is possible without the offer. Title-call safe: the announcement is server-derived text, so a title-call hit would still prove harness MCP works.
use_tool never issued on the cc wire (escaped-form 0-hit — the tools[] schema presence of use_tool does NOT count) — model did not take the MCP-call path; probe meaningless for this cell.
no use_tool call targeted codegraph__codegraph_explore (escaped FQ-name 0-hit — the prompt's plain mention does NOT count) — the declared MCP target was never called; probe meaningless.
the declared echo command was never issued (escaped command 0-hit) — plain tool path not exercised; probe meaningless.
